entries.proposition: The epileptic absence strain has a SMALLER T-type current than its non-epileptic control in relay neurons, not a larger one: peak T-type current density at P7 to P9 is about 15.9 versus about 21.2 pA per pF (p < 0.05), with Cav3.1 mRNA and protein reduced in adult tissue; a high-voltage current is slightly increased.
entries.snippet: Interestingly, VB neuron T-type current density was found to be significantly decreased in P7–P9 GAERS compared to NEC at membrane potentials between −60 and −40 mV
entries.anchor: Results, T-type calcium current density is decreased in GAERS VB neurons

entries.proposition: Relay-neuron burst firing is suppressed in the epileptic strain, in adult and pre-epileptic animals under long hyperpolarisation, and the authors attribute this mainly to an increased Ih current, with the reduced T-type current making no significant contribution once Ih is blocked.
entries.snippet: The decreased T-type current density might contribute to the suppressed burst-firing in GAERS, although since a non-significant increase was observed for the current injection required to burst-fire between NEC and GAERS in the presence of Ih blockade (Fig. 6b), it appears that the small decrease in T-type current density has no significant contribution.

entries.proposition: The authors write that what part, if any, the ventrobasal neurons play in absence-seizure propagation remains to be elucidated in the genetic absence model.
entries.snippet: What part, if any, VB neurons play in absence seizure propagation thus remains to be elucidated for the GAERS genetic model of absence seizures.

entries.proposition: The authors note a prior gain-of-function Cav3.2 variant in the epileptic strain (restricted to reticular neurons, not relay neurons) and an earlier study that found no strain difference in T-type current in acutely dissociated cells and one that found increased Cav3.1 mRNA by in-situ hybridisation; they explain their discrepancy by preparation (intact slice versus dissociated cells, current density versus absolute current) and say a dissection error could affect the P9 mRNA comparison.
entries.snippet: This contrasts our findings of reduced T-type calcium current density in GAERS VB neurons.

entries.proposition: Figure 5 read as an image: panel b T-type current density curves for the non-epileptic control (filled squares) peak about -21 pA per pF at -50 mV against about -16 for GAERS (open circles) with stars from -60 to -40 mV, and the Z944 curve near 0; panel c high-voltage current slightly larger in GAERS at -10 to 0 mV; panel e Cav3.1 mRNA about 1.6 versus 1.2 (two stars); panel g Cav3.1 protein about 3.7 versus 1.7 (three stars); panel a burst firing present before and abolished by Z944.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 5b: NEC peak about -21, GAERS about -16 pA/pF, stars -60 to -40 mV; Figure 5g: Cav3.1/vinculin about 3.7 versus about 1.7, three stars.
entries.anchor: Figure 5 panels a to g; deposit jpg as delivered

entries.proposition: Figure 1 read as an image: current threshold for rebound burst after a 200 ms hyperpolarisation is about minus 27 pA in adult controls against about minus 48 pA in the absence strain (two stars) and about minus 45 against minus 43 pA at P15 to P20 (no star); action potentials per burst about 4 to 5 in all groups; input resistance lower in the absence strain at both ages (one star each); resting potential about minus 73 mV in all groups.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1b-e: adult burst threshold NEC about -27 vs GAERS about -48 pA (**); P15-20 about -45 vs -43; APs/burst about 4-5; Rin lower in GAERS (*); Vrest about -73 mV.

entries.proposition: Figure 2 read as an image: with a 1000 ms hyperpolarisation the threshold current is about minus 30 against minus 41 pA at P15 to P20 and about minus 33 against minus 57 pA in adults (one star each); action potentials per burst about 4 in all groups; burst action-potential frequency about 300 to 450 Hz and tonic firing curves overlap in the two strains.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2b-g: 1000 ms threshold NEC about -30 vs GAERS -41 pA (P15-20, *), about -33 vs -57 pA (adult, *); APs/burst about 4; burst frequency and tonic firing overlap.

entries.proposition: Figure 3 read as an image (ZD7288-subtracted tail current density): at P15 to P20 the absence strain has about minus 5.9 against about minus 3.3 pA/pF at minus 110 mV, with stars across minus 110 to minus 60 mV; in adults about minus 8.8 against about minus 6.2 pA/pF with stars from minus 110 to minus 90 mV; the normalised curves differ only at P15 to P20 near minus 75 mV.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3b-e: Ih tail density at -110 mV: P15-20 GAERS about -5.9 vs NEC -3.3 pA/pF; adult about -8.8 vs -6.2 pA/pF (stars).

entries.proposition: Figure 4 read as an image (Western blots, six animals per strain, vinculin-normalised): HCN1 about 1.52 against about 0.96 (one star) and HCN3 about 0.60 against about 0.30 (one star) higher in the absence strain; HCN2 about 0.77 against 0.80 and HCN4 about 0.04 in both, no difference.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4b: HCN1 GAERS about 1.52 vs NEC 0.96 (*); HCN3 about 0.60 vs 0.30 (*); HCN2 and HCN4 no difference.

entries.proposition: Figure 6 read as an image (ZD7288 present): the burst threshold becomes depolarising and similar in the two strains (about plus 30 and plus 38 pA at P15 to P20; about plus 59 and plus 62 pA in adults; no star), action potentials per burst about 4, input resistance no longer different and resting potential about minus 90 mV in all groups.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 6b-e: with ZD7288 burst threshold NEC about +30 vs GAERS +38 pA (P15-20); about +59 vs +62 (adult); no star; Vrest about -90 mV.
